profile.reading:
This is Noovle DC Rivoli, one of three new data center buildings that TIM's cloud subsidiary Noovle S.p.A. built in the Turin metropolitan area, the other two sited in Moncalieri and Settimo Torinese. An engineering case study from Italian design and BIM firm Open Building, working alongside mechanical and electrical engineer Deerns Italia on a project referred to internally as The Rooster, documents a 2021 through 2022 conversion of an industrial site of about 19,500 square meters in Rivoli into a data center for Noovle. The project converted an existing warehouse, described as having a basement and a ground floor, into data hall space, added new mechanical, electrical, and plumbing systems in the surrounding outdoor area, and included a separate four story building with its own basement on the same plot, all delivered under Open Building's integrated BIM based design process. Neither Noovle's own announcements nor the engineering case study disclose a specific IT power capacity in megawatts, technical floor area, or an independently verified Tier rating for this Rivoli building on its own, an honest gap this registry records rather than a guess.

Noovle S.p.A. is the cloud computing arm of Italian telecom group TIM, operating under TIM's enterprise division, and this Rivoli site forms part of the data center infrastructure Noovle built to host Google Cloud's Turin region, the second Google Cloud region in Italy after Milan, which Google's own announcement dates as available from March 23, 2023 with three availability zones. Google's announcement of the Turin region does not name Rivoli specifically, describing the underlying infrastructure only as hosted across Noovle's national data center network, while TIM's own technical newsletter separately describes that broader Noovle network, of which Rivoli is one part, as spanning 16 data centers across Italy with about 40,000 square meters of combined floor space, 60,000 servers, and 40 megawatts of total IT electrical power, an aggregate figure across all Noovle sites nationwide rather than a number for this Rivoli building specifically, so this registry records it as a campus wide note rather than assigning it to this one building.

Independent research commissioned by the University of Turin, reported in regional trade press, projects that Noovle's three new Turin area data centers in Rivoli, Moncalieri, and Settimo, developed together with partners Google Cloud and Intesa Sanpaolo, could generate roughly 1.7 billion euro in regional economic value and around 30,000 jobs across a combined two year construction phase and three year operational phase, a regional economic projection rather than a fact about this specific building's technical specifications. Rivoli itself sits on Turin's western outskirts and has a long history as an industrial and manufacturing town, which fits Noovle's approach here of converting an existing industrial warehouse into a data center rather than building new on greenfield land, an approach the company has repeated at other sites in its Turin area buildout.
profile.research_note: Rewritten 2026-09-06 to remove banned aggregator sources (datacentermap.com) present in the prior version of this row, and to correct an error in the prior draft, which named the sibling Turin-area sites as "Cebrosa and Moncalieri." Regional trade press (italia40-plus.it, covering University of Turin research) names the three new Noovle Turin-area sites as Rivoli, Moncalieri, and Settimo (Torinese), not Cebrosa. datacentermap.com and datacenters.com were checked for cross reference (address, site name) but excluded as citations per house rules. No source found gives a per-building MW, sqm, or verified Tier rating for this Rivoli building specifically, an honest gap stated in the reading rather than filled with a network-wide or campus-wide number. WebSearch quota was exhausted partway through this session's research, so this write relied on WebFetch of previously identified URLs and could not run additional targeted queries (e.g. for a possible Tier certificate or municipal permit record specific to Rivoli).
profile.campus_power_note: TIM technical newsletter reports the wider Noovle network (16 data centers nationwide including this Rivoli site) totaling about 40,000 sqm, 60,000 servers, and 40 MW total IT electrical power. This is a network-wide aggregate, not a per-building figure, so it is not applied to any single numeric field for this facility.
